title: Brief gap-junction blockade makes G. dorotocephala regenerate other species' head shapes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Brief gap-junction blockade makes G. dorotocephala regenerate other species' head shapes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In decapitated Girardia dorotocephala fragments, a transient perturbation of cell-to-cell physiological connectivity with the gap junction blocker octanol can lead to regenerated heads whose shapes stochastically match those of other planarian species (Schmidtea mediterranea, Dugesia japonica, Polycelis felina).

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › Abstract

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: after decapitation in G. dorotocephala, a transient perturbation of physiological connectivity among cells (using the gap junction blocker octanol) can result in regenerated heads with quite different shapes, stochastically matching other known species of planaria (S. mediterranea, D. japonica, and P. felina)

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M, Durant F, Hammelman J, Bessonov N, Volpert V, Morokuma J, Pinet K, Adams DS, Pietak A, Lobo D, Levin M, “Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms”, International journal of molecular sciences (2015), doi:10.3390/ijms161126065; section “Abstract”. Scope: Regenerating pre-tail fragments of genetically wild-type Girardia dorotocephala treated with octanol (123 µM, 3 days)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-girardia-01: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.69

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The phenotype and intervention are directly measurable, and published images and counts allow a limited audit. Full confirmation or refutation would require the underlying specimen-level image set or an independent public replication.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Classify blinded day-10 head images from octanol-treated and control fragments against reference species and compare phenotype frequencies. The treatment must produce discrete cross-species-like shapes absent from controls.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Visual species matching can be observer-dependent.

Individual-level raw images and treatment records are not clearly deposited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.55
analysis feasibility: 0.8
data adequacy: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.65
operationalizability: 0.95

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Head shape after a stated octanol regimen is a clear experimental variable, and the paper reports the outcome with group sizes. The images are figures rather than a deposited landmark set, and no independent public replication supplies the same perturbation and readout. Confirming or refuting the species match requires those records or a new assay.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On decapitated Girardia dorotocephala pre-tail fragments, compare blinded head-shape classes after 123 µM octanol for three days with water controls, using landmarks against reference Schmidtea, Dugesia, and Polycelis heads. Stochastic assignment to those reference shapes, absent in controls, would support the result; only wild-type or disorganized heads would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Individual images and landmark coordinates are not in a public repository.

Species labels were assigned by resemblance before quantitative comparison.
